_readme: The model-facing action registry. Each entry becomes one tool the model may call. tier: auto = runs without asking, ask = needs the user's approval, blocked = never runs. primary = the argument that permission rules in permissions.json match against, e.g. switch_model(coding). kind = command means the primary argument is a shell line and gets split and checked part by part (src/core/permissions.js). A rule in permissions.json can move an action between auto and ask, but nothing can lift a blocked action.

actions.name: switch_model
actions.description: Switch JARVIS to another model preset when the user asks for it (for example 'use the coding model'). The next reply comes from the new model.

actions.name: open_whiteboard
actions.description: Switch the window to whiteboard mode (the empty board where panels are placed).

actions.name: close_whiteboard
actions.description: Leave whiteboard mode and go back to the HUD. Panels are kept for next time.

actions.name: open_panel
actions.description: Open a new tab in the workspace beside the chat. Give it a title; content is optional and may be filled in later by calling this again with the same id.

id.description: Optional kebab-case id. Reusing an id updates that panel instead of making a new one.

content.description: Panel content, formatted as the type requires. May be empty.

lang.description: Language name, only for type code.

actions.name: open_system_panel
actions.description: Open the built-in system panel (GPU memory, load, temperature, generation speed, context use).

actions.name: close_panel
actions.description: Close a floating panel on the whiteboard by its id (or the built-in system panel by the id 'system'). The panel's content stays in the conversation.

actions.name: list_dir
actions.description: List the files and folders of the project folder (or a subfolder). Shows file sizes. Skips the contents of node_modules, .git, target, dist.

path.description: Folder, relative to the project folder. Default: the project folder itself.

depth.description: How many levels to show, 1 to 4. Default 1.

actions.name: read_file
actions.description: Read a text file from the project. Lines come back numbered. Long files are read in pages: use offset and limit to continue.

path.description: File path, relative to the project folder.

offset.description: First line to read, starting at 1.

limit.description: How many lines, at most 1000. Default 300.

actions.name: search_files
actions.description: Search the project's text files for a regular expression. Returns file:line: text. Case-insensitive unless the pattern contains an upper-case letter.

path.description: Folder or file to search, relative to the project folder. Default: everything.

glob.description: Only files whose name matches, for example *.js (* and ? only).

actions.name: edit_file
actions.description: Change a file by replacing exact text. old_text must appear in the file exactly once (copy it from read_file, without the line numbers) unless replace_all is true. Prefer this over write_file for changes to existing files.

path.description: File path, relative to the project folder.

old_text.description: The exact text to replace, whitespace included.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring exactly one.

actions.name: write_file
actions.description: Create a file, or replace a whole file, with the given content. Parent folders are created. For small changes to an existing file use edit_file.

path.description: File path, relative to the project folder.

actions.name: run_command
actions.description: Run one shell command in the project folder and return its output and exit code. Runs in PowerShell on Windows, sh elsewhere. Use it for tests, builds, git and similar; use the file tools to read or change files. The user may be asked to approve it. Commands time out after 30 seconds unless timeout_secs is given (at most 300).

actions.name: set_tasks
actions.description: Keep a visible task checklist for a job with several steps. Send the WHOLE list every time (it replaces the old one). Statuses: todo, doing, done; at most one task is doing. Update it as you finish each step, so the user can see progress.

tasks.description: The full list, in order. Each item: {"text": "what to do", "status": "todo|doing|done"}.

actions.name: submit_plan
actions.description: Plan mode only: hand the user your plan for approval. Give a one-line summary and the ordered steps. Nothing is changed until the user approves; if they reject it, they will tell you what to change.

summary.description: One line: what the plan achieves.

steps.description: Ordered steps, each one concrete action as a string.

actions.name: use_skill
actions.description: Load the instructions of a skill listed in <skills> and follow them. Use it when the task matches a skill's description.
